question: You cut a recording, dropped in a second clip, music and a title. What should Command S do?
context: A video edit is now many clips, sounds, titles and captions on tracks, not one trimmed recording. Save As will write a project you can reopen (being built now). The question is only what the Command S key does on a video.

options.label: Command S saves the project
options.summary: Command S always saves your edit as a Photonz project you can open again. The recordings you used are never changed. Export is how you get a video file to send.
pros: Works the same for one clip or twenty
Your original recordings are never written over
It is what Premiere and Final Cut do, so an editor never has to learn it
cons: Trim a recording and send it now takes an Export, where the old recording window did it with one Command S
options.mitigation: Export stays in the File menu and on the close sheet, so trim and send is two steps, never a hunt.

options.label: A plain trim writes the recording
options.summary: If all you did is trim one recording, Command S writes the shorter recording back over the file, as the old recording window did, with the original kept beside it. Anything more (a second clip, a title, captions, music) saves a project.
pros: Trim and send stays one press
Nothing about a bigger edit is ever lost
cons: Command S means two different things depending on what you did, and the window has to say which one it is about to do
options.mitigation: The title bar and the File menu name what Save will write before you press it.

options.label: Not now
options.summary: Keep Command S dimmed on a video. Save As writes a project, and Export writes a video, and nothing else changes.
cons: Command S does nothing on the thing you spend longest on
options.mitigation: Save As is in the File menu and on the close sheet.
